Do any Videos exist of Nicolas Tesla? 

No known surviving motion-picture footage (video) of Nikola Tesla exists.
Tesla (1856–1943) lived well into the age of film and newsreels. Written accounts indicate he appeared in short newsreels in the 1920s–1930s and helped produce a technical film around 1935 that was offered to Paramount (described as visually and sonically effective but too technical for them). However, none of this material is known to have survived in accessible form—no confirmed digitized footage of him has been identified in archives, newsreel collections, or elsewhere.
Reliable sources, including documentaries (such as a DW production) and articles examining the topic, explicitly note the absence of known surviving film of Tesla, as well as no confirmed voice recordings. Occasional claims circulating online (including some labeled “the only footage” or “believed to show” him at an event like a birthday press conference) refer to blurry, low-quality, or unconfirmed clips that do not match verified historical records or clear visual identification.
What does exist in abundance:
•  Many still photographs (including famous ones from his Colorado Springs lab experiments, which were promotional double exposures).
•  Modern documentaries, dramatizations, animations, and reenactments (e.g., PBS’s American Experience: Tesla, the 1980 film The Secret of Nikola Tesla, and various YouTube history videos).
In short, while Tesla was a public figure and film technology was available during his later life, no authentic moving images of him are known to have been preserved.
